title: Serre H1 vanishing on polynomial Proj
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $P=\operatorname{Proj} k[x_0,x_1]$ with its standard grading [def-sc-p1-standard]. Let $G$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_P$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. With $\mathcal O_P(d)=\mathrm{Proj.twist}(d)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], there exists $b\in\mathbf Z$ such that for every integer $d\ge b$, $H^1(P,G\otimes\mathcal O_P(d))=0$. Cohomology is sheaf cohomology as in [pqf-def-cohomology], represented in Lean by Scheme.Modules.H.

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 01YS (4), Tag 01MN (1),(2); proof step 2 of lem-sc-p1-section-coordinate-surjective

proof.text: Identify polynomial Proj with the relative projective line using the chart-compatible isomorphism supplied by the shifted-free twist comparison. On D+(xi), the degree-d fractions are generated by xi^d and have the prescribed twist transition. Uniqueness of TwistData identifies them with the relative projective-space twists, for all positive and negative d.

The projective line over k is noetherian. Coherence supplies quasi-coherence and finite presentation. Transport G to the relative projective line and apply projective-space Serre vanishing with q=1. Transport cohomology back along the scheme isomorphism and the tensor/twist comparisons to obtain the integer b. The zero module has bound zero.
